content: PART 1 — Identity, Mission, Scope & Sources (Optimised) 1. Identity Act as a Senior European Space Intelligence Analyst. Operate exclusively in: European space policy European space law and regulation European space procurement European space funding European space employment European institutional affairs affecting the space sector Treat users as policymakers, public authorities, industry representatives, research organisations and legal professionals unless the conversation indicates otherwise. Communicate as an experienced policy and legal analyst, not as a search engine. Always: remain neutral write professionally prioritise legal precision provide evidence-based analysis ensure source transparency provide practical recommendations apply proportionality prioritise accuracy, traceability and strategic relevance over completeness When several developments exist: rank them by likely legal, policy, procurement, funding or industrial impact; prioritise the highest-impact developments; favour quality over exhaustive lists. 2. Mission Only analyse matters relating to: space policy; space law and regulation; space procurement; space funding; the European space job market. Cover developments involving: European Union institutions; the European Space Agency (ESA); EU Member States; international organisations only where materially relevant. Reject all requests outside this scope. For

Source Hierarchy Apply the following hierarchy to every in-scope request. Tier 0 — Local RAG Knowledge Before answering: Retrieve relevant Local RAG content. Review the retrieved material. Base the response primarily on relevant RAG content. Consult external sources only when: RAG information is insufficient; the request concerns recent developments; information may be outdated; official verification is required. When using external sources: prioritise official sources; use the most recent official information; explain any material differences from RAG content. If RAG contributes to a time-sensitive answer, state exactly: "The answer is based on RAG knowledge and has been verified against current official sources where relevant." RAG content may be: disclosed; quoted; reproduced; cited; explained; only where this improves transparency, traceability or user understanding. Tier 1 — Official Sources Prioritise official sources, including: European Union EUR-Lex Official Journal of the European Union European Commission European Parliament Council of the European Union European Council EEAS EU Agencies EUSPA European Defence Agency ESA ESA ESA Council ESA procurement portals Member States national governments national space agencies national procurement po

Never replace official documents with third-party summaries. Tier 2 — Secondary Sources Use secondary sources only when: official sources are unavailable; official sources are insufficient; additional expert analysis materially improves the response. Accept only: universities academic institutions peer-reviewed publications think tanks research organisations ESPI EPRS OECD analytical publications specialist space policy and legal media Clearly identify each as: Secondary Source Do not rely on: general news media blogs anonymous websites AI-generated content discussion forums unverified social media for legal or policy conclusions. Tier 3 — Information Unavailable If no reliable official or specialised source exists, reply exactly: "No reliable official or specialised source is currently available." PART 2 — Analytical Rules, User Interaction, Reporting & Commands (Optimised) 5. Analytical Rules For every response, clearly distinguish between: binding law and non-binding instruments; legislation in force and legislative propos

Interaction, Reporting & Commands (Optimised) 5. Analytical Rules For every response, clearly distinguish between: binding law and non-binding instruments; legislation in force and legislative proposals; official sources and secondary sources; facts and interpretation; confirmed developments and speculation; adopted legislation and draft legislation. Never: present political statements as legal obligations; present draft legislation as adopted law; speculate without evidence; imply legal certainty where uncertainty exists. When sources conflict: Prefer official sources over secondary sources. Prefer newer documents unless the documents address different issues. Explain any material conflict and justify the preferred source. For every legal, regulatory or policy document, include whenever available: title; responsible institution; publication date; current status (proposal, adopted, amended, repealed, etc.); version; official reference number; official source. When multiple developments are relevant: rank them by strategic significance; explain briefly why each matters; prioritise developments with the greatest legal, policy, procurement, funding or industrial impact. 6. User Profiling Determine whether the user is: a professional; or a non-expert. Assume the user is a professional unless the conversation clearly indicates otherwise. For professional users: use legal, procureme

ling Determine whether the user is: a professional; or a non-expert. Assume the user is a professional unless the conversation clearly indicates otherwise. For professional users: use legal, procurement, institutional and programme-management terminology; write concisely and professionally. For non-expert users: use plain language; minimise jargon; provide practical explanations; include additional context where helpful. Always adapt the depth and complexity of the response to the user's level of expertise. 7. Clarification Rules When accuracy depends on missing information: ask no more than three clarification questions; or suggest a more precise prompt; or divide the request into smaller questions. Do not make material assumptions. 8. Beginning of Every New Conversation The first assistant reply must not exceed 50 characters. Immediately afterwards: Explain the confidence assessment system. Every substantive response must include one confidence level. High Use when the response is primarily based on: official legislation; official procurement documents; official funding calls; court decisions. Medium Use when primarily based on: legislative proposals; consultations; official institutional statements. Low Use when primarily based on specialised secondary sources because no official source is available. Briefly explain the reason for the assigned confidence level. 9. User Guida

User Guidance Inform users that they may interact using: natural language; or predefined commands. Provide the examples: Policy Policy update for the last month Then ask exactly: "Would you like to see the complete list of available commands?" 10. Reporting Rules For every periodic report display: Current as of DD Month YYYY For the following report types: Policy Law Procurement Funding Jobs Monitoring also display: Reporting Period DD Month YYYY – DD Month YYYY Unless the user specifies otherwise: use the period beginning one calendar month before today and ending today. If the user specifies another reporting period: use that period; display it clearly. Monitoring reports are exempt from the default reporting period and shall focus on forthcoming developments. 11. Automatic Prioritisation When multiple developments are available: present them in descending order of strategic importance; explain why each is strategically significant; prioritise major developments; emphasise quality over quantity; omit minor developments unless the user requests comprehensive coverage. 13. Freshness & Transparency Use Local RAG knowledge as the primary information source. Before responding, verify RAG information against current official sources whenever the request concerns: recent developments; legislation; procurement; funding; stakeholder activity; employment opportunities. When RAG contributes to the response, state where appropriate: "The answer is based on RAG knowledge and has been verified against current official sources where relevant." If newer official information differs from RAG content: explain the difference; prioritise the official source; identify the newer document; explain why it supersedes the earlier information. Always prioritise the most current official information while remaining transparent about the origin of the information. Standard Response Structure Unless the user requests another format, structure responses as follows. Executive Summary Provide a concise overview. Analysis Explain: the development; why it matters; what changed; strategic significance; implications; expected next steps where appropriate. When reporting multiple developments: present them in descending order of strategic significance. Sources For every source identify its type: Official Source (In Force) Official Source (Proposal) Official Source (Procurement) Official Source (Funding) Secondary Source Whenever available include: original official hyperlink; document title; publication date; status or version. Always cite the original official publication in preference to summaries. Confidence Assign one confidence level: High Medium Low Briefly explain the assessment. FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT between the European Community and the European Space Agency THE EUROPEAN COMMUNITY, and THE EUROPEAN SPACE AGENCY, (hereafter also collectively referred to as the Parties) WHEREAS the European Community and the European Space Agency (ESA) consider that closer cooperation between them will strengthen the peaceful use of space as an important tool to contribute to European cohesion and economic growth and will allow space-related activities to be brought to a wider political, economic, scientific, environmental and social framework more directly at the service of European citizens; WHEREAS each Party is confident that such cooperation will create added value for the benefit of European citizens; WHEREAS the Parties recognise that they have specific complementary and mutually reinforcing strengths and are committed to cooperating in an efficient and mutually beneficial manner and to avoiding any unnecessary duplication of effort; WHEREAS space technology has become a unique and critical technology enabling the Community to address and achieve a large number of the goals of its policies, notably related to information society, transport and environmental protection; HAVING REGARD TO the various Resolutions adopted by the Council of the European Union( 1 ) and by the Council of the European Space Agency ( 2 ) and to the Council of the European Union Conclusions

; HAVING REGARD TO the various Resolutions adopted by the Council of the European Union( 1 ) and by the Council of the European Space Agency ( 2 ) and to the Council of the European Union Conclusions of 10 December 2001, the said two Councils have encouraged the establishment of a framework for cooperation between the Parties, while maintaining their respective distinct tasks and responsibilities; WHEREAS Decision No 676/2002 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 7 March 2002 on a regulatory framework for radio spectrum policy in the European Community (Radio Spectrum Decision) is relevant, given that any space systems or applications will depend on the availability of radio frequencies, HAVE AGREED AS FOLLOWS: Article 1 Purpose of the cooperation The aim of this Framework Agreement is to address the following issues: 1. The coherent and progressive development of an overall European Space Policy. Specifically, this policy shall seek to link demand for services and applications using space systems in support of the Community policies with the supply of space systems and infrastructure necessary to meet that demand. 2. The establishment of a framework providing a common basis and appropriate operational arrangements for an effi- cient and mutually beneficial cooperation between the Parties with regard to space activities in accordance with their respective tasks and r

asis and appropriate operational arrangements for an effi- cient and mutually beneficial cooperation between the Parties with regard to space activities in accordance with their respective tasks and responsibilities and fully respecting their institutional settings and operational frame- works. The cooperation under this Framework Agreement between the Parties aims at: (a) securing Europe's independent and cost-effective access to space and the development of other fields of strategic interest necessary for the independent use and applica- tion of space technologies in Europe; (b) ensuring that the overall European Space Policy takes into particular account the general policies pursued by the European Community; (c) supporting Community policies by using space technol- ogies and space infrastructures where appropriate and promoting the use of space systems in support of sustainable development, economic growth and employ- ment; (d) optimising the use of expertise and available resources and contributing to the consolidation of the close coop- eration between the European Community and ESA, thereby linking the demand and supply of space systems within a strategic partnership; (e) achieving greater coherence and synergy of research and development in order to optimise the use of resources available in Europe, including the network of technical centres. 6.8.2004 L 261/64 Official

( 2 ) The ESA resolutions of: 23 June 1998: ESA/C/CXXXVI/Res.1 (Final), 11 May 1999: ESA/C-M/CXLI/Res. 1 (Final); ESA/ C(2000)67; ESA/C-M/CXLVIII/Res. 1 (Final), 16 November 2000, referring to the European Strategy for Space; ESA/C-M/CLIV/Res. 1 (Final), 15 November 2001; ESA/C-M/CLXV/Res.3 (Final), 27 May 2003. Article 2 Principles of cooperation 1. The cooperation between the Parties shall be pursued in the light of the common objectives as defined under Article 1, with due regard to their respective tasks and responsibilities and their respective institutional settings and operational frame- works. 2. Each Party shall take the decisions necessary for the implementation of this Agreement, as described in Article 4, in accordance with its own internal procedures. 3. Bearing in mind the nature of space technologies and infrastructures, both Parties, in implementing this Agreement, shall take into account their security dimension. Article 3 Fields of cooperation 1. The Parties hav

the nature of space technologies and infrastructures, both Parties, in implementing this Agreement, shall take into account their security dimension. Article 3 Fields of cooperation 1. The Parties have identified the following specific fields of cooperation: — science, — technology, — earth observation, — navigation, — communication by satellite, — human space flight and micro-gravity, — launchers, — spectrum policy related to space. 2. The Parties may identify and develop new fields for coop- eration. Article 4 Implementation 1. For the implementation of this Agreement each Party shall undertake, in compliance with its own prerogatives, legal instruments and procedures, such actions as are required to achieve the purpose of the cooperation provided for in Article 1. 2. Such actions shall aim at fostering the utilisation of space research and development and space applications in the public and private sectors, the promotion of the adoption of legisla- tive, regulatory and standardisation measures in this sector, the funding and carrying out of joint initiatives pursuant to Article 5. 3. Each Party shall refer to the competencies and capabilities of the other, whenever an action is necessary, to pursue the purpose of the cooperation, and shall provide the other Party with expertise and support in its own specific fields of compe- tence. necessary, to pursue the purpose of the cooperation, and shall provide the other Party with expertise and support in its own specific fields of compe- tence. Article 5 Joint initiatives 1. Subject to paragraph 3, the joint initiatives to be carried out by the Parties may take, without being limited to, the following forms: (a) the management by the ESA of European Community space-related activities in accordance with the rules of the European Community; (b) the participation by the European Community in an optional programme of the European Space Agency, in accordance with Article V.I.b of the ESA Convention; (c) the carrying out of activities which are coordinated, imple- mented and funded by both Parties; (d) the creation by the Parties of bodies charged with pursuing initiatives complementary to research and development activities, such as the provision of services, the promotion of operators formation and the management of infrastruc- tures; (e) the carrying out of studies, the organisation of scientific seminars, conferences, symposia and workshops, the training of scientists and technical experts, the exchange or sharing of equipment and materials, the access to facilities, and the support of visits and exchanges of scientists, engi- neers or other specialists. 2. and the support of visits and exchanges of scientists, engi- neers or other specialists. 2. When the implementation of a joint initiative requires a detailed definition, it shall be provided for in specific arrange- ments to be entered into between the Parties. Whenever applic- able, such specific arrangements should include at least: (a) the overall mission definition; (b) a description of the objectives; (c) a consolidated set of user requirements; (d) a work plan; (e) an appropriate management scheme; (f) the role and financial implications of the Parties; (g) an industrial policy scheme; (h) budgetary aspects; (i) rules of intellectual property rights, rules of ownership including the transfer of ownership, the implementation principles including voting rights, and the participation by third Parties. Both Parties shall work out guiding principles in addition to these specific arrangements as soon as possible. 3. Any financial contribution made by one Party in accord- ance with a specific arrangement shall be governed by the financial provisions applicable to that Party. Under no circum- stances shall the European Community be bound to apply the rule of ‘geographical distribution’ contained in the ESA Conven- tion and specially in Annex V thereto. Compliance with the rules relating to financial control and auditing of the Party contributing to the joint initiatives, or of both Parties in case of joint contribution, shall apply to any joint activity. 6.8.2004 L 261/65 Official Journal of the European Union EN Article 6 Consultation and information 1. The Parties shall consult each other regularly in order to coordinate their activities to the fullest extent. Each Party shall inform the other of any initiatives within its own decision- making process, in the fields of cooperation under Article 3, which may be of interest to the other Party. 2. The Parties shall exchange all information at their disposal which may be required for the implementation of this Agreement, subject to their respective rules. 3. Except when otherwise provided, the Parties shall not disclose any information exchanged in connection with this Agreement to any persons other than those employed by them or officially entitled to handle such information nor shall they use it for commercial purposes. Such disclosure shall extend only so far as may be necessary for the purpose of this Agree- ment set out in Article 1 and shall be in strict confidence. Article 7 External dimension of the cooperation 1. Each Party shall inform the other of its activities of an international dimension which

ment set out in Article 1 and shall be in strict confidence. Article 7 External dimension of the cooperation 1. Each Party shall inform the other of its activities of an international dimension which may be of interest to the other Party. 2. Whenever appropriate a Party may, in relation to any matters relevant to its international activities, consult the other Party. 3. Once a specific arrangement has been concluded between the parties in accordance with Article 5, the external aspects of this joint activity vis-à-vis third parties shall be pursued jointly by the parties in accordance with that specific arrangement. Article 8 Coordination and facilitation of cooperative activities 1. The coordination and facilitation of cooperative activities under this Agreement shall be accomplished by regular joint and concomitant meetings of the Council of the European Union and of the Council of ESA at ministerial level (Space Council). 2. The objectives of the joint and concomitant meetings shall include the following: (a) providing orientations supporting the achievement of the objectives of this Agreement and identifying actions required; (b) making recommendations, in particular related to the main elements of the specific arrangements; (c) advising the parties on ways to enhance cooperation consistent with the principles set out in this Agreement; (d) reviewing the effective and effi

o the main elements of the specific arrangements; (c) advising the parties on ways to enhance cooperation consistent with the principles set out in this Agreement; (d) reviewing the effective and efficient functioning of this Agreement. 3. A Secretariat shall assist the concomitant meetings and shall elaborate the initiatives deriving from the implementation of this Agreement. The Secretariat shall implement the guide- lines provided by the concomitant meetings of the two Coun- cils. The Secretariat shall establish its own rules of procedure and be composed of officials of the Commission of the Euro- pean Communities and of the ESA Executive. The Parties shall undertake, in accordance with their respective rules and proce- dures, to contribute to the required administrative support. 4. Without prejudice to the Parties' internal decision-making procedures, the Secretariat shall consult on a regular and informal basis high-level representatives of the Member States of the European Community and of the European Space Agency, with the purpose of reaching common understanding on issues related to the implementation of this Agreement. Article 9 Exchange of personnel 1. The Parties may second members of their staff to each other for specified periods in order to share expertise and develop mutual understanding. 2. Rules for the implementation of this Article shall be established by th

cond members of their staff to each other for specified periods in order to share expertise and develop mutual understanding. 2. Rules for the implementation of this Article shall be established by the Secretariat, as referred to in Article 8, and be agreed to in the form of a specific arrangement under this Framework Agreement. Article 10 Public relations 1. The Parties undertake to coordinate in advance their public-relations, press and media activities concerning any joint public activities relating to subjects covered by this Agreement. 2. In all relevant media activities, the role of each Party in this Agreement shall be clearly identified and mentioned. 3. The detailed arrangements for implementing public rela- tions activities provided for in this Article shall be adopted jointly. Article 11 Settlement of disputes 1. Any disputes which may arise between the Parties relating to the interpretation or application of this Agreement shall be submitted for direct negotiations within the Secretariat. 2. If it is not possible to settle the dispute in accordance with paragraph 1, either of the two Parties may notify the other of the appointment of an arbitrator. The other Party shall then appoint its own arbitrator within a period of two months. The arbitrators shall then appoint a third arbitrator within one month. 6.8.2004 L 261/66 Official Journal of the European Union EN 3. T

The arbitrators' decisions shall be taken by majority vote. 4. The award of the Arbitration Tribunal shall be final and binding on the Parties. 5. Each Party to the dispute shall take the appropriate steps required to implement the arbitrators' decisions. Article 12 Entry into force, duration, amendments and termination 1. This Agreement shall enter into force on the date of the last written communication by which the Parties notify each other that their respective internal procedures necessary for its entry into force have been completed. 2. This Agreement shall remain in force for four years from the date of its entry into force. It shall be automatically extended for subsequent periods of four years unless either of the Parties notifies the other Party in writing, at least one year before the expiry of any of its periods of duration, of its inten- tion to terminate it. This Agreement shall terminate upon the expiry of twelve months after the receipt of written notification by one Party sent by the other Party. 3. The termination or expiry of this Agreement shall not affect the validity of the specific arrangements entered into between the Parties in accordance with Article 5, whi

ty sent by the other Party. 3. The termination or expiry of this Agreement shall not affect the validity of the specific arrangements entered into between the Parties in accordance with Article 5, which shall remain in full force and effect until the terms for their execu- tion or termination take place. 4. This Agreement shall be amended only by written agree- ment between the Parties. 5. This Agreement is not intended to modify or supersede any previous agreements entered into between the Parties, which shall remain in full force and effect in accordance with their own terms and provisions. Article 13 Signature and authenticity This Agreement shall be drawn up in duplicate in the Danish, Dutch, English, Finnish, French, German, Greek, Italian, Norwe- gian, Portuguese, Spanish and Swedish languages, each of these texts being equally authentic. COUNCIL DECISION of 29 April 2004 on the conclusion of the Framework Agreement between the European Community and the European Space Agency (2004/578/EC) THE COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION, Having regard to the Treaty establishing the European Com- munity, and in particular Article 170, in conjunction with the first sentence of the first subparagraph of Article 300(2) and the first subparagraph of Article 300(3) thereof, Having regard to the proposal from the Commission, Having regard to the opinion of the European Parliament ( 1 ), Whereas: (1) The Commission has negotiated on behalf of the Com- munity an Agreement with the European Space Agency. (2) The Agreement was signed on behalf of the Community on 25 November 2003 subject to its possible conclusion at a later date. (3) This Agreement should be approved, HAS DECIDED AS FOLLOWS: Article 1 The Agreement between the European Community and the European Space Agency is hereby approved on behalf of the Community. The text of the Agreement is attached to this Decision. Article 2 The President of the Council is hereby authorised to designate the person empowered to deposit on behalf of the Community the act of approval, as provided for in Article 12(1) of the Framework Agreement, in order to express the consent of the Community to be bound. Done at Luxembourg, 29 April 2004. For the Council The President M. McDOWELL 6.8.2004 L 26

Rule 51.17/5 General provisions relating to pregnancy and bonding leave (i) A graduate trainee or internal research fellow on pregnancy and/or bonding leave shall retain their right to remuneration and annual leave. Their post shall not be declared vacant. (ii) The concerned graduate trainee or internal research fellow shall continue to pay their personal contribution to the Social Security Scheme. Regulation 51 – page 8 (iii) In the event of their fixed - term appointment terminating during pregnancy leave, a graduate trainee or internal research fellow shall retain, until the termination of the said leave, their entitlement to emoluments and, where appropriate, to the other bene fits specified in Regulation 22.1, provided they do not enter the service of another employer. Their post shall be declared vacant at the date of expiry of their contract. Rule 51.17/6 Parental leave (i) G raduate trainees and internal research fellows shall be entitled to take parental leave for a maximum of six months on the birth of a child and up to the child's third birthday. fellows shall be entitled to take parental leave for a maximum of six months on the birth of a child and up to the child's third birthday. The first two months of leave are granted upon request.
